**Answer**

> *“Most famous” is a matter of taste and context, but here’s a quick snapshot of the American composers who have left an indelible mark on music history—whether in classical, film, Broadway, or popular genres.*

| Composer | Era / Genre | Why They’re Famous |
|----------|-------------|--------------------|
| **George Gershwin** (1898‑1937) | Jazz‑Classical crossover | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” – bridged jazz idioms with symphonic form. |
| **Aaron Copland** (1900‑1990) | Classical | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” – his “American sound” defined mid‑20th‑century orchestral music. |
| **Leonard Bernstein** (1918‑1990) | Classical & Broadway | “West Side Story,” “Candide” – a conductor, composer, and charismatic educator. |
| **John Williams** (born 1942) | Film | “Star Wars,” “Indiana Jones,” “Jurassic Park” – arguably the most recognizable film score composer of all time. |
| **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | Minimalism | “Einstein on the Beach,” “Glassworks” – a pioneer of minimal music, influencing countless contemporary composers. |
| **Samuel Barber** (1910‑1981) | Classical | “Adagio for Strings,” “Knoxville: Summer of 1915” – known for lyrical, emotionally resonant works. |
| **John Philip Sousa** (1854‑1932) | March music | “The Stars and Stripes Forever” – the “March King” whose marches remain staples of American patriotic music. |
| **Stephen Sondheim** (1930‑2021) | Musical theatre | “Sweeney Todd,” “Into the Woods” – revolutionized Broadway with complex lyrics and sophisticated harmonies. |
| **Charles Ives** (1874‑1954) | Experimental | “The Unanswered Question,” “Concord Sonata” – early modernist blending of American folk tunes with avant‑garde techniques. |
| **William Grant Still** (1895‑1978) | Classical | “Afro-American Symphony” – first major symphony by an African‑American composer, championed racial equality in music. |
| **John Adams** (born 1947) | Contemporary | “Short Ride in a Fast Machine,” “Nixon in China” – a leading figure in post‑minimalism. |

### Quick Takeaways

* **Broadway & Film**: Sondheim, Bernstein, Williams, Gershwin, Copland.
* **Classical & Orchestral**: Copland, Barber, Sousa, Still, Ives, Adams.
* **Contemporary & Minimalist**: Glass, Adams, Philip Glass.
